module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.Free
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.PushforwardContinuous
public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Sites.CoversTop.Basic

@[expose] public section

universe u v

namespace SheafOfModules

open CategoryTheory Limits

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
variable {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
variable {R : Sheaf J RingCat} (M : SheafOfModules R)
variable [∀ (X : C), (J.over X).HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat AddCommGrpCat)]
variable [∀ (X : C), HasWeakSheafify (J.over X) AddCommGrpCat]
variable [∀ (X : C), (J.over X).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat]

/-- A vector bundle is a sheaf of modules that is locally isomorphic to
a free sheaf. -/
structure VectorBundleData (M : SheafOfModules.{v} R) where
  /-- The index type for the open cover on which the vector bundle is free. -/
  OpensIndex : Type u
  /-- The indexed family of opens on which the vector bundle is free. -/
  opens : OpensIndex → C
  /-- The indexed family of opens covers the base. -/
  coversTop : J.CoversTop opens
  /-- The indexed family of types that index local bases for the vector bundle. -/
  BasisIndex : OpensIndex → Type v
  /-- The restriction of the vector bundle to one of the opens is free. -/
  locallyFree : ∀ i, (M.over <| opens i) ≅ SheafOfModules.free (BasisIndex i)

structure FiniteRankVectorBundleData (M : SheafOfModules R) extends VectorBundleData M where
  /-- The predicate that every local basis in the defining data of the vector bundle is finite. -/
  finite : ∀ i, Finite (BasisIndex i)

/-- A class for vector bundles of constant finite rank. -/
class IsVectorBundleWithRank (M : SheafOfModules R) (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The predicate that a sheaf of modules is locally free. -/
  exists_vector_bundle_data : ∃ (D : M.FiniteRankVectorBundleData),
    ∀ i, Nat.card (D.BasisIndex i) = n

end SheafOfModules

reformulations.difference: Local freeness is represented by a covering family of site objects and explicit isomorphisms on over-sites, rather than pointwise open neighborhoods or Mathlib's local generators with an IsIso predicate.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a topological space, Mathlib's Opens.coversTop_iff identifies CoversTop with an open cover, and Opens.sheafEquivOver identifies over-site restriction with ordinary restriction. An inverse local trivialization gives generating sections whose canonical map is an isomorphism; conversely, an invertible generator map gives the required trivialization. The scratch file proves Nonempty M.VectorBundleData ↔ M.IsLocallyFree.

reformulations.difference: Finiteness is attached to each chosen local basis; the definition does not impose a globally constant rank or a uniform rank bound.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: This is exactly finite local freeness in Stacks Definition 17.14.1(2), which allows the finite index set to vary with the neighborhood. The scratch file proves equivalence with the existence of Mathlib local-generator data satisfying both IsLocallyFreeData and IsFiniteType on that same cover.

reformulations.difference: Constant rank n is expressed using arbitrary finite local basis types with Nat.card equal to n, instead of using a fixed n-element basis type.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Each finite basis type of cardinality n is equivalent to Fin n; applying freeFunctor to this equivalence reindexes the free sheaf. Conversely, use ULift (Fin n) on every member of the cover. The scratch file proves the resulting iff for every n, including zero. The inherited finite field excludes Nat.card's infinite-type default.

reformulations.difference: The conclusion asks for a categorical coproduct decomposition into two bundles, neither isomorphic to the original bundle, rather than explicitly saying 'a direct sum of two line bundles'.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The induced category is the full subcategory of constant finite-rank locally free sheaves, which is closed under finite direct sums, so its coproducts are ordinary direct sums. On nonempty connected complex projective space, ranks are well-defined and additive. A decomposition of a rank-two bundle has summand ranks adding to two. A rank-zero summand would be zero and make the other summand isomorphic to the original bundle, contradicting non_trivial. Both summands therefore have rank one. Conversely, two rank-one summands cannot be isomorphic to the rank-two original bundle.

review.notes: All three declarations and all their use sites were checked. The only problem-file user is HartshorneConjecture.lean, which uses the fixed finite-rank class, not the unrestricted data type. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles without errors or sorry dependencies: it proves the three library equivalences, constructs free bundles of every finite rank, identifies the free rank-zero object as zero, proves that a finite local basis of Nat.card zero is empty, and checks that an empty open cover covers exactly an empty space. Thus the empty-base behavior is the standard pointwise-vacuous behavior, not a defect. The unrestricted data type's allowance of infinite local bases is consistent with its local-freeness meaning and is explicitly narrowed by the following definitions. Access limitation: Project Euclid and AMS returned challenge pages for Hartshorne's 1974 paper, so its exact Conjecture 6.3 wording was not directly inspected; the independently cited MathOverflow source explicitly gives the rank-two, n ≥ 7, two-line-bundle statement used in the comparison.
